branchName.instructions: Use lowercase kebab-case branch names with one of these prefixes: feat/, fix/, refactor/, eval/, test/, docs/, chore/. Keep names concise and describe the actual change. Examples: feat/async-ticket-evidence, fix/golden-partial-evidence, eval/graph-rag-benchmark. Do not include AI/agent names.

commitMessage.instructions: Use Conventional Commits. Format: <type>(optional-scope): <concise imperative summary>. Allowed types: feat, fix, refactor, perf, test, docs, eval, chore. Keep the subject concise, describe the actual repository change, and do not mention AI, Codex, AGY, or generated code. Add a body only when useful for explaining behavior, safety, migration, or evaluation impact.

pullRequest.instructions:
Generate a concise PR title using Conventional Commit style.

The PR description should use this structure:

## Summary
Explain what changed and why.

## Key Changes
List only meaningful implementation and architecture changes.

## Validation
Report only tests and evaluation results that were actually executed. Include Golden 300, behavior gate, retrieval gate, hard-negative gate, full pytest, and production gate when relevant.

## Safety / Regression
Describe impact on ACL, tenant isolation, memory, citations, guardrails, HITL, tool execution, and web research when relevant.

## Performance
Include measured before/after results only when a benchmark was actually run. Clearly distinguish controlled benchmarks from production end-to-end measurements.

## Deferred / Known Limitations
Document non-blocking limitations or experiment-only features.

Never claim a test passed unless verified from execution. Never change or hide failing results. Do not mention AI, Codex, AGY, or agent-generated code in the PR title or description.
